subject: Re: Reliability & SLO comparison - follow-up and next tests
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-25T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: Reliability / SLO comparison - post-call recap

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the call this morning — really helpful to hear the SRE perspective and current baseline at Acme. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have alignment: 

Recap from our discovery call:
- Acme current baseline: using Hyperscaler-X managed inference endpoints for production; target uptime SLA 99.95% for customer-facing features, internal SLO at 99.9% with a 30-day error budget.
- Key concerns you called out: regional failover behavior, long-tail rate limiting under bursts, and visibility into error budget consumption across routes.
- Primary success metrics you care about: p50/p95/p99 latency under sustained load, system availability (no silent degradation), and predictable rate-limit behavior (429 + Retry-After).

How Redwood differentiates (brief):
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and isolation.
- Smart routing + fallbacks: automated fallback to compatible model variants and cross-region routing when a pool degrades.
- Observability: token-level cost/latency breakdowns and per-route error-budget tracking.
- Circuit breakers and graceful degradation: configurable error thresholds and automatic throttles vs total service outage.

Proposed next tests for validation:
1) Baseline throughput test (30–60 minutes): sustained 200 RPS, measure p50/p95/p99 and error rate.
2) Failover simulation: take the primary AZ out of route, observe failover time, error spike, and recovery window.
3) Rate-limit stress: burst traffic with long-tail to validate 429 behavior and Retry-After accuracy.
4) Error-budget burn analysis: simulate transient backend errors to see whether alerting and fallbacks trigger as expected.

What we need from you to move forward:
- Confirm SRE contact to include in the technical sync (I included Tom above; please confirm).
- Share any internal acceptance criteria or additional metrics (e.g., max acceptable p99, warmup thresholds).
- Approve a 30-minute technical sync next week for Marcus to run through the failover plan and test harness.

I attached an initial Redwood SLO matrix and a proposed test plan template for quick review (redwood-slo-matrix.pdf, redwood-failover-test-plan.docx).

If that looks good I can have Marcus schedule the technical session and we can pick concrete windows for tests (we typically do staging runs outside your business hours).

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0128

Attachments:
- redwood-slo-matrix.pdf (summary of Redwood SLOs and per-route guarantees)
- redwood-failover-test-plan.docx (test template)

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for the clear recap and proposed tests. Quick responses inline below: 

- Confirming Tom (cc'd) is our SRE lead and will coordinate the test windows and provide any internal failure injection guidance.
- Our current acceptance criteria: p99 <= 350ms for the inference path under typical load; 99.95% availability for production endpoints; internal tolerance at 99.9% for staging.
- We do use Hyperscaler-X for production with autoscaling, but we've seen noisy neighbor and long warm-up issues when scaling beyond 150 RPS in the EU region. Our primary concern is cross-region failover behavior and ensuring requests don't silently queue or timeout during failover.

I've attached our current SLO doc for reference (acme-current-slos.pdf). Please note we have regulatory customers that require documented failover behavior within 60s and for error codes to be explicit so downstream retry logic can work.

Tom — could you and the team confirm availability for a technical sync next week? Prefer Wed/Thu morning PST.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Product Operations | Acme AI
elena.torres@acmeai.com

Date: 2026-02-27T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Reliability / SLO comparison - next steps and test plan

Elena / Tom —

Appreciate the SLO doc — helpful context. Marcus (cc) will lead the technical sync and run the test harness. A few clarifications and how Redwood maps to your acceptance criteria: 

1) Availability vs error budget: for Dedicated deployments we offer a predictable pool with an SLA target (we can sign to 99.95% for a Dedicated pool with contractual terms) and an internal error-budget model per route that triggers automatic throttles and fallbacks. That means we can guarantee cross-region routing and a controlled fallback path (not a silent queue) when a pool is degraded.

2) Rate limiting and warm-up: our serving runtime supports pre-warmed pools and dynamic burst capacity; for the worst-case warm-up we recommend a two-step warmup (50% throughput for 5 min then 100%) to avoid transient long tails. We'll include a warmup plan in the test script.

3) Failover behavior: our default is to failover to a compatible model variant in another region within the same tier (e.g., quantized variant) rather than attempting a live transfer of a warm KV cache. Typical observed failover recovery is under 30–45s for region fallback; we'll measure this in the test and instrument both sides for traces.

Proposed technical sync agenda (30 min):
- 5m: Introductions & goals
- 10m: Marcus walks through test harness and failover steps
- 10m: Agree test windows and acceptance criteria
- 5m: Next steps / schedule

Marcus — can you propose two windows Wed/Thu morning PST (Tom preferred) and confirm the harness link and any credentials needed? I'll coordinate on the Redwood side and we can include a short checklist for SRE-level permissions (ability to trigger failover, read-only access to metrics).

Thanks — I'll also attach a concise SLO comparison matrix to make it easy to share with your SREs.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-03-03T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Test scenarios and metrics - Redwood failover & rate-limit validation

Hi all —

Thanks for looping me in. Below is a concrete, SRE-oriented plan I'll cover in the sync and hand off as a runnable script for your team. The goal is to produce repeatable measurements we can attach to the PO as acceptance evidence.

Test scenarios (runnable):
A) Baseline throughput test (30–60m):
  - Target: steady 200 RPS
  - Measure: p50/p95/p99 latency, request error rate, token cost distribution
  - Success: p99 <= 350ms and error rate < 0.5% under steady-state

B) Failover simulation (15–30m):
  - Method: route failure injection (simulate AZ loss) or explicitly remove primary pool from routing
  - Measure: failover start-to-stable (time until p95 returns to baseline), transient error spike, percentage of requests that returned explicit 5xx vs allowed fallback responses
  - Success: failover recovery < 45s, no silent queueing, clear 429/5xx classification where applicable

C) Rate-limit stress test (burst + long-tail, 30m):
  - Method: burst to 500 RPS for 2 minutes, then sustained 250 RPS with long-tail clients
  - Measure: observed 429s, Retry-After correctness, tail latency behavior, and error-budget burn rate
  - Success: graceful throttling (429 with Retry-After), retry semantics allow client recovery without silent loss of requests

Measurement & instrumentation:
- We'll provide a small client harness (k6 + simple tracing wrapper) and a read-only dashboard to capture metrics.
- We'll collect request ids, traces, and error logs and share a summarized report.

Acceptance / error-budget criteria (proposal):
- Over a 1-hour window across tests, error-budget consumption must be < 5% (per your internal definition).
- Dedicated pool availability measured at 99.5% during testing windows (we can adjust for contractual SLA language later).
- Failover recovery < 30s preferred, up to 45s acceptable with documented fallbacks.

Next steps:
1) Confirm technical sync window (Wed 03/04 09:30 PST or Thu 03/05 09:30 PST)  - I can hold both.
2) Tom / Acme SRE: confirm the ability to trigger routing changes or allow Redwood to run the simulated failover in a controlled window.
3) We will hand over the k6 harness and a runbook 24 hours before the test window.

Happy to adjust thresholds - wanted to put a concrete draft on the table so Acme has something to sign off against.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
